source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT VA3 publishes 16 MW of IT capacity. Among the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that publish a megawatt figure, VA3 ranks sixteenth out of nineteen, representing roughly 1.2 percent of the 1,326 MW published across the state. Virginia hosts 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the overwhelming majority publish no capacity figure at all, so the state total is a floor, not a ceiling.

At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 16 MW of IT load is roughly 1,600 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density more typical of GPU training clusters, the same 16 MW supports roughly 400 racks. At 700 W per H100, 400 racks at that density would hold on the order of 22,800 accelerators. These are assumptions about rack density, not NTT's claims, and the operator does not publish a rack count or a supported workload type on the page this site read.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications this site holds for VA3, so none can be read for what they qualify the campus to host. The campus sits in Ashburn, the densest data center corridor in Virginia and one of the most interconnected in the world, but interconnection depth and available fiber are not published on the spec page and cannot be stated as facts here. At 16 MW, VA3 is a mid-small facility in its own state context, relevant to colocation buyers but not, on published figures alone, a facility that moves the needle on AI scaling at the regional level.
